newsitem.title: UK: Author of salacious Fergie book denies revenge.
newsitem.headline: Author of salacious Fergie book denies revenge.

text.p: The author of a book revealing intimate details about the Duchess of York's sex life on Thursday denied he wrote it out of spite, saying instead he thought the work would help people understand her.

Allan Starkie was a close friend of the Duchess, better known as Fergie, and her lover John Bryan. But Starkie fell out with them after he was jailed without charge for five months in Germany over the collapse of the company he ran with Bryan.

In his book "Fergie, Her Secret Life," published on Thursday, he says he blames the Duchess for his imprisonment because she had allegedly failed to pay money she had pledged to one of the company's creditors.
Nevertheless, Starkie denied revenge was his motive for writing the book.

"Revenge would be too simple a word for it -- it would have been too easy," Starkie told a news conference in a crowded London book shop where the tome was launched. "What I really wanted was for her to be seen in a complete light."
Starkie, a diminutive New Yorker with a pronounced lisp, kept detailed diaries from the moment he was introduced to Fergie in 1992 by Bryan, who was already her lover.

His story begins before that -- Starkie alleges Fergie first betrayed her husband, Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew, just three years after their marriage while she was pregnant with her second daughter.
The affair with Texan Steve Wyatt lasted for two years, he says. As soon as Wyatt left London, Fergie embarked on her relationship with Bryan, according to Starkie.
Their affair was revealed to the world in 1992 when a newspaper published photographs showing them half-naked and cavorting beside a swimming pool in the south of France.
Most famously, Bryan was pictured sucking Fergie's toes -- a fact Bryan hotly denies, said Starkie. "I wasn't sucking her toes," he quotes Bryan as saying. "I was licking them."
The author said he acted as a go-between between Fergie and Bryan during their volatile four-year relationship and in the book he portrays a self-centred, egotistical and greedy couple.
Fergie berates her lover for failing to address her as Duchess, while Bryan is verbally abusive to her. They have sex while under the same roof as Prince Andrew.

The Duchess placed great faith in clairvoyants, who at one point convinced her that Prince Charles would not become Britain's next king, raising in her absurd hopes that she could become queen although estranged from her husband.

One of her more bizarre notions, Starkie claims, is that she was destined to become America's first lady by marrying John F. Kennedy Junior -- son of the assassinated president -- even though she had never met him.

After the collapse of the German company, Starkie tried to commit suicide. He says Fergie had been told by one of her mystics that he would succeed in killing himself at a second attempt and she asked him to do her a favour in the next life.

"When you're dead, would you find JFK and explain to him that I am destined to marry John-John (John Kennedy Junior)...I would like him (JFK) to help me with this and approach John-John in his dreams and try to...convince him," Starkie quotes the Duchess as saying.

Fergie, whose own autobiography is due to be published next week, had tried to stop Starkie from publishing his book but she pulled out of a legal case after it became clear she might have to give evidence in court. She is reported to have huge debts.
